subject: Syncore Health — latency mapping, token envelope, and concurrency playbook
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Parker <emma.parker@syncorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Syncore Health — latency mapping, token envelope, and concurrency playbook

Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a pragmatic plan to validate SLOs and token limits so we can scope Dedicated capacity correctly. TL;DR: we need 1) a concrete latency/throughput target matrix, 2) a small perf run with real sample prompts + expected output sizes, and 3) a canary/capacity plan for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.

Context from call (summary):
- Use case: clinical triage assistant that ingests patient notes (avg input ~400 tokens, 90th pct = 1,100 tokens) and returns structured summary + suggested ICD codes (output avg ~120 tokens, 95th pct = 350 tokens).
- Expected peak concurrency: 120 concurrent users during clinic hours; estimated steady qps ~40, burst qps up to 250 for async batch jobs.
- Latency targets: product team needs 95th <= 400ms for short sessions (<512 tokens) and acceptable 95th <= 1.2s for long sessions (~1,500 tokens) with streaming preferred for UI responsiveness.

Immediate asks / next steps (action owners):
1) Syncore: provide representative prompt set and a few worst-case long messages (Emma) — due Mon 10/05.
2) Redwood: run a short perf pass on our dev Dedicated pool with 64 concurrency and 4-shard batching to produce p50/p95/p99 traces (Marissa) — plan by 10/06.
3) Tech alignment: Neha/Dev will propose KV-cache + prefix caching recommendations and model variant fallback (e.g., 7B quantized for burst) — note due 10/06.

Notes on tradeoffs to consider up front:
- Token envelope: combining long inputs with long outputs multiplies latency; we should measure input-only and output-only tails.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces perceived latency for the UI but increases sustained throughput and KV cache pressure.
- Batching improves throughput but increases per-request latency headroom — we'll recommend smart batching windows and per-route overrides.

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (skeleton SLO matrix); mock-latency-trace-20261003.txt (sample p95 trace from earlier demo).

Proposed meeting: 30-min sync Wed 10/06 09:00 PT to review perf results and finalize canary criteria. Is that OK for your team?

Thanks,

Logan Wright

- For batch jobs (overnight coding of claims), latency is less critical but throughput is — we want to understand the per-token cost at scaled throughput (10k requests / night).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Parker <emma.parker@syncorehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 20:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Syncore Health — latency mapping, token envelope, and concurrency playbook

Thanks Emma — appreciate the prompt turn. For technical transparency I've sketched a plan for the perf run and what we'll measure:

Perf run plan (dev Dedicated):
- Workload slices: short (<=512 in / <=128 out), medium (~800 in / ~200 out), long (>1,000 in / >400 out).
- Concurrency targets: smoke at 16, test at 64, stress at 192 (to validate autoscaling behavior).
- Models: baseline 13B float model (no quant), 13B q4f16 (low-cost burst), and a streaming-optimized small variant (7B q4) as fallback.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency for token-emit and end-to-end, tail CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, and per-request token counts.

Important measurement notes:
- Head-first streaming: we'll instrument to capture time-to-first-token per request; if the model supports chunked emit, we can deliver UI header within target while continuing generation. That reduces perceived latency even if end-to-end is longer.
- Batching window policy: we'll test 0ms (no batching), 10ms, and 25ms to show latency vs throughput curvature; expect throughput gains but higher p95 for short requests at >10ms.
- Canary criteria: 95th token-emit <= 350ms for short slice on baseline; fallback to 7B streaming variant if p95 > 450ms for >2 minutes under steady qps.

Actionable output from perf run: 1) a latency matrix mapping input/output token envelopes to p50/p95/p99; 2) recommended per-route batching window and model variant fallback; 3) estimated token cost table for projected nightly batch volume.

I'll run the perf pass Monday afternoon and share raw traces + a short write-up before our Wed sync. Dev / Neha: please comment on caching strategy and fallback sizing below.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Syncore Health — latency mapping, token envelope, and concurrency playbook

On Sat, Oct 03, 2026 at 8:48 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> For technical transparency I've sketched a plan for the perf run and what we'll measure:
> 
> Perf run plan (dev Dedicated):
> - Workload slices: short (<=512 in / <=128 out), medium (~800 in / ~200 out), long (>1,000 in / >400 out).

All — a few practical hedges and a proposed fallback matrix from the infra side:

1) KV / prefix caching: for triage flows we should persist recent patient context (when allowed by Syncore policy) to reduce effective input token counts on follow-ups. Recommend TTL 30m and per-patient cache key. If caching reduces avg input by 60% for follow-ups, we move many requests into the short slice which is huge for p95 latency.

2) Model variant routing: propose the following policy (can be per-route):
- PRIMARY: 13B q4f16 (balanced).
- FALLBACK-1 (burst): 7B streaming q4 (lower latency tail for short interactive requests).
- FALLBACK-2 (batch): 13B quantized batch path with aggressive batching windows for overnight jobs.

3) Concurrency and autoscale: set a soft concurrency cap per node to avoid head-of-line blocking when a few long jobs occupy shards — prefer per-route circuit-breaker at 256 concurrent requests with automatic spillover to batch queue.

4) Instrumentation: include time-to-first-token and token-emission-rate in traces; capture one representative slow trace per 10k requests for offline analysis (attach to ticket).

Next technical deliverables (who/when):
- Marissa: run perf pass (10/05) and drop traces to Drive.
- Dev: produce a simple canary runbook and thresholds for system alerts (10/06).
- Emma/Syncore: drop sample prompts + expected outputs (10/05).

If these look good I'll add the fallback matrix to the SLO worksheet and include estimated cost deltas for each routing policy.

-Neha Kapoor
Staff Engineer, Performance & Serving, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

> Emma: looping you in on the technical hedges so procurement and product can align on what's being measured and why.
